members.summary: How `lucid.peft.get_peft_model` adapts a model with multitask prompt tuning.
members.extended:
Multitask prompt tuning (Wang et al., 2023, [arXiv:2303.02861](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.02861)) learns one
prompt shared by every task and, per task, a low-rank factor pair
$u_k \in \mathbb{R}^{L \times r}$, $v_k \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d}$.
Task $k$'s prompt is the shared one multiplied elementwise by
$u_k v_k$, so a new task adds $r\,(L + d)$ numbers, and a prompt
trained on source tasks can start a target task (`prompt_tuning_init` and
`prompt_tuning_init_state_dict_path`).  Which task each row of a batch is
comes from the `task_ids` argument of the model's call.

Field names, their order, defaults and `adapter_config.json` are the reference adapter
library's.  The prompt tuning fields
(`num_virtual_tokens`, `tokenizer_name_or_path`, …) hold as for
`lucid.peft.PromptTuningConfig`.

parameters.name: prompt_tuning_init_state_dict_path
parameters.description:
A `.safetensors` adapter file of a multitask prompt trained on the source
tasks; required by the three source initialisations.

parameters.name: prompt_tuning_init_task
parameters.description: With `"EXACT_SOURCE_TASK"`, the source task whose factors are taken.

parameters.name: num_ranks
parameters.description: The rank $r$ of each task's factor pair.

parameters.name: num_tasks
parameters.description: How many tasks the prompt serves.

raises.description: A field holds a value of the wrong type.
A count is not positive, or `"TEXT"` lacks its text or tokenizer.

examples:
>>> from lucid.peft import MultitaskPromptTuningConfig
>>> config = MultitaskPromptTuningConfig(num_virtual_tokens=8, num_tasks=3, num_ranks=2)
>>> config.peft_type, config.num_tasks
(<PeftType.MULTITASK_PROMPT_TUNING: 'MULTITASK_PROMPT_TUNING'>, 3)
>>> MultitaskPromptTuningConfig.from_dict(config.to_dict()) == config
True

methods.summary: Build the shared prompt and each task's low-rank pair.
methods.extended:
The pair is $u_k$ and $v_k$ for each of `config.num_tasks` tasks; the
shared prompt starts as `PromptEmbedding`'s does, or from a source-task prompt
when `config.prompt_tuning_init` asks.

parameters.name: tasks
parameters.description: The task id of each row, `(batch,)`.

methods.name: forward
methods.signature: forward(indices: Tensor, task_ids: Tensor | None = None)
methods.summary: The prompt of each row's task: `(B, rows)` ids and `(B,)` task ids to `(B, rows, token_dim)`.

raises.description: `task_ids` is missing, or is not one integer per row.
A task id is not in `[0, num_tasks)`.

members.summary: The prompt of multitask prompt tuning: a shared prompt scaled by a low-rank factor pair per task.
members.extended:
For a row of task $k$ the prompt is `embedding(ids) * (cols[k] @ rows[k])` —
the shared `(num_virtual_tokens, token_dim)` prompt times the product of
`(num_virtual_tokens, num_ranks)` and `(num_ranks, token_dim)` factors.

parameters.name: config
parameters.description:
Sizes (`num_virtual_tokens`, `num_transformer_submodules` and
`token_dim` set), the tasks and ranks, and the initialisation.

parameters.name: word_embeddings
parameters.description: The model's token table, which `"TEXT"` copies rows of.

raises.description:
A source initialisation without `prompt_tuning_init_state_dict_path`, a source file
that is not `.safetensors`, lacks a tensor, or whose shapes do not fit this adapter.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import MultitaskPromptEmbedding, MultitaskPromptTuningConfig
>>> config = MultitaskPromptTuningConfig(
...     num_virtual_tokens=3, token_dim=8, num_transformer_submodules=1, num_tasks=2
... )
>>> prompt = MultitaskPromptEmbedding(config, nn.Embedding(10, 8))
>>> prompt(lucid.arange(3).long().reshape(1, 3), lucid.tensor([1])).shape
(1, 3, 8)

summary: `lucid.peft.tuners.multitask_prompt_tuning` — multitask prompt tuning, a prompt per task.
extended:
Multitask prompt tuning (Wang et al., 2023, [arXiv:2303.02861](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.02861)) learns one prompt shared by every task
and, per task $k$, a low-rank pair $u_k$, $v_k$; the task's prompt is the shared
one multiplied elementwise by $u_k v_k$.  A new task adds $r\,(L + d)$ numbers, and a
prompt trained on source tasks can start a target task (`MultitaskPromptTuningInit`).  Which task
each row of a batch is comes from the `task_ids` argument of the model's call.  Pick it when
several related tasks share one model and each should cost little.

The prompt is applied by hooks on the model's own call.  Here: `MultitaskPromptEmbedding` (what is
learned) and `MultitaskPromptTuningModel` (the tuner).  `MultitaskPromptTuningConfig` and
`MultitaskPromptTuningInit` are here too and exported from `lucid.peft`.
citation: Wang, Zhen, et al. "Multitask Prompt Tuning Enables Parameter-Efficient Transfer Learning." [arXiv:2303.02861](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.02861), 2023.
